subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Religion Ethics Through A Study Of Christianity Spec B
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which religious concept teaches that humans should care for the environment as carers, not owners?
options: Indifference
Stewardship
Materialism
Dominion as exploitation
questions.explain: Stewardship is the belief that humans have a duty to look after the Earth on God's behalf.

questions.q: Which is a non-religious (e.g. Humanist) view on the origins of the universe?
options: The universe was created in six literal days
The universe does not exist
The universe arose through natural processes such as the Big Bang, without a creator
God personally shaped each planet
questions.explain: Humanists generally explain the universe through scientific processes rather than a divine creator.

options: A fertility treatment helping couples conceive
An environmental policy
A form of capital punishment
A type of euthanasia
questions.explain: IVF (in-vitro fertilisation) is a fertility treatment that helps couples who struggle to conceive.

questions.q: When Jesus was asked for the greatest commandment, he taught that people should:
options: Give all their money to the poor
Avoid eating certain foods
Keep the Sabbath above all else
Love God and love your neighbour as yourself
questions.explain: Jesus summarised the law as loving God with all your heart and loving your neighbour as yourself.

questions.q: Which view best reflects a 'pro-life' position on abortion?
options: That the foetus is not alive at any stage
That the unborn child has a right to life from conception
That life only begins at adulthood
That abortion is always the woman's free choice
questions.explain: The pro-life position holds that human life begins at conception and should be protected.

questions.q: Which view supports the use of animals in some circumstances within many religious traditions?
options: That humans have stewardship over animals and may use them responsibly
That animals must never be touched
That animals are worthless
That animals have no role in creation
questions.explain: Many traditions allow responsible use of animals while still teaching kindness and care towards them.

questions.q: How might a religious believer reconcile belief in creation with the Big Bang theory?
options: By denying the universe exists
By suggesting God could be the cause behind the Big Bang
By rejecting all science
By claiming science and faith can never overlap in any way
questions.explain: Many believers argue the Big Bang could be the means by which God created the universe, so the two can coexist.

questions.q: The Parable of the Good Samaritan mainly teaches Christians to:
options: Become priests or Levites
Show love and care to anyone in need
Only help people from their own community
Travel to Jerusalem on pilgrimage
questions.explain: The parable teaches that a true neighbour shows compassion to anyone in need, regardless of background.

questions.q: The Incarnation is the Christian belief that:
options: Jesus went up to heaven
Souls are reborn into new bodies
God became human in the person of Jesus
Jesus rose from the dead
questions.explain: The Incarnation is the belief that God took on human form as Jesus Christ.

questions.q: The 'problem of evil' challenges Christians because it asks how:
options: A good, all-powerful God can allow suffering
Heaven and hell can both exist
Evil can be enjoyable
Humans invented religion
questions.explain: The problem of evil questions how an omnipotent and benevolent God can permit evil and suffering.

options: Being saved from sin and given eternal life with God
The first book of the Bible
A medieval monastery
A type of church service
questions.explain: Salvation is being saved from sin and its consequences, gaining eternal life with God.

questions.q: In Christianity, 'grace' is best understood as:
options: A reward earned by attending church
God's undeserved love and forgiveness freely given
The skill of living a holy life
A prayer said before meals only
questions.explain: Grace is God's free, unearned love and forgiveness offered to humanity.
